paper.title_en: Fast implementation of controlled $\pi $ phase gate using superadiabatic shortcuts with Rydberg superatoms
paper.abstract_en: Quantum phase gates serve as core fundamental resources for quantum information processing, and their preparation efficiency and structural stability directly determine the overall performance of quantum computing and quantum communication. The traditional adiabatic preparation method is prone to the influence of decoherence due to its excessive time consumption, while superadiabatic shortcut technology can significantly shorten the evolution time while retaining the advantages of the adiabatic process. In this paper, we propose a scheme for rapidly implementing a quantum phase gate by combining superadiabatic scheme and quantum Zeno dynamics to construct shortcuts to adiabatic passage. We demonstrate the superadiabatic shortcut by using Rydberg superatoms in a distant-atom-cavity system. Furthermore, we utilize the controlled $\pi $ phase gate to achieve the preparation of N-particle cluster state. In addition, the effects of decoherence and operational errors induced by various parameters are discussed. Numerical simulation demonstrates the proposed scheme has high fidelities and robustness against both cavity leakage and atomic spontaneous emission. Different from previous superadiabatic shortcut schemes, our protocol adopts second-order iterative counterdiabatic driving to avoid experimentally inaccessible direct couplings, where the counterdiabatic correction is realized merely by reshaping feasible Gaussian laser pulses. Furthermore, we analyze the scalability of cascaded controlled $\pi $ phase gate for generating N-particle cluster state under realistic decoherence sources.
